input.source_text: mut calls = 0; class A { public fun migrate_revision(old, new) -> Object { calls = calls + 1; nil } } let a = A.new(); module M { public fun run() -> Object { let opened = A.open() { |t| t.define_method(:m) { 2 } }; let before = calls; let explicit = a.migrate_revision(1, 2); let refused = try { Reflection::Class.reactivate(A, 1) } catch e { e }; [before, explicit, calls, refused] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. Two of the three halves already held and were measured: a commit performs NO implicit enumeration, so `calls` is 0 before any explicit call, and the instance's own `migrate_revision` answers nil when application code calls it. What was absent is the reactivation refusal. C016 makes a ClassRevision read-only and forbids user code from reactivating one, and C020 requires a rollback to publish a NEW validated revision instead, so the surface now EXISTS in order to refuse rather than being absent and answering an unrelated missing-message error.
